summary: The most likely cause is the aa-sync deploy at 11:19 (aa-sync-00633, 'normalize holdings payload v2'). Starting at 11:20:04, portfolio-consumer rejects messages on the portfolio-updates queue because they carry the field 'positions' where its schema expects 'holdings'. Rejected messages are redelivered and then dead-lettered. The dead-letter queue reached 2500, redeliveries climbed to about 22/s, consume_rate fell to 18.483, and portfolio-consumer err_rate reached 0.604. The producer-side payload change is the root cause and the consumer's strict validation is the failure point. The log sample is truncated (180 matches, 30 shown), and I did not confirm why only about half of users are affected.

hypotheses.statement: aa-sync-00633 changed the published holdings payload (field 'holdings' renamed to 'positions'). portfolio-consumer's strict schema rejects these messages, which are then redelivered and dead-lettered.
hypotheses.label: high

supporting.text: aa-sync deployed a payload-format change one minute before the first consumer errors
portfolio-consumer rejects messages on a field-name mismatch, starting right after the deploy
aa-sync publishes to portfolio-updates and portfolio-consumer consumes from it
The dead-letter queue grew to 2500 on the portfolio-updates queue
Redeliveries rose sharply, consistent with repeated rejection
Publish rate stayed steady while consume rate fell, so this is not a producer outage
portfolio-consumer error rate rose to 0.604 while latency stayed flat, which points to validation rejects rather than slowness

hypotheses.statement: portfolio-consumer-00091 (10:50, 'log level tweak') contributed to the failure. This is unlikely given the 30-minute gap before onset and the nature of the change.
hypotheses.label: low

supporting.text: portfolio-consumer also had a deploy at 10:50, described as a log level tweak, well before onset

unresolved: Why only about half of users are affected: a partial aa-sync rollout, a mix of payload types, or only some message types changed. This was not verified.
The log sample covers only 30 of 180 matching errors, so I did not check whether other error types exist later in the window.
Whether messages with the old 'holdings' field are still being processed successfully was not verified.
portfolio-consumer-00091 is very likely unrelated, but its diff was not inspected.

actions.text: Roll back aa-sync-00633, or ship a hotfix that emits 'holdings' (or both field names) in the portfolio-updates payload.
actions.rationale: This removes the schema mismatch that triggers the rejections at the source.

actions.text: After the producer is fixed, replay the dead-lettered messages from the portfolio-updates DLQ to portfolio-consumer. Check first whether the 'positions' messages need transformation.
actions.rationale: About 2500 portfolio updates are stuck in the DLQ and users are missing them.

actions.text: Add schema versioning and a contract test between aa-sync and portfolio-consumer, and consider making the consumer tolerate both field names during migrations.
actions.rationale: A producer-side payload change broke the consumer with no gate or compatibility layer.

actions.text: Alert on portfolio-updates DLQ growth and on consumer err_rate.
actions.rationale: The incident was reported about 30 minutes after onset.
